checks.ref:
command:change=$(find openspec/changes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -name archive)
review="$change/review-code.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-code stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R1 (SUGGESTION, packages/client/src/test/features/locations/steps/locationsShortcutE2eHelpers.ts:3) is not worth fixing and its Fix is harmful: the cited rule .claude/rules/code-style.md explicitly exempts tests ('Strings in tests (test descriptions, mock data) — acceptable'), the finding itself rates the impact 'Low stakes while the key is `/`', and the proposed fix (import KeyboardKey.SLASH into the E2E steps) makes the aria-keyshortcuts assertion at locations_search_shortcut_e2e.steps.ts:121-124 and the key presses compare production code against itself, so a wrong change to KeyboardKey.SLASH would pass every E2E scenario although the spec requires literally `aria-keyshortcuts="/"` and pressing `/`. 'Fix risk: none' is therefore not honest. The finding is also applied inconsistently: it ignores the same pattern in the same file ('ArrowDown'/'Enter' literals at steps :76-77 while KeyboardKey.ARROW_DOWN/ENTER exist), and the unit test AddLocationButton.test.tsx:34 also uses the literal '/'. Drop R1, set the SUGGESTION count to 0 and keep the Ready verdict.
